To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fabrication of plasmonic nano-structures by fs-laser irradiation of ZnO/Ag nanorods can be used to increase the photocurrent in solar hydrogen generation.
plasmonics embedded at the interface between a semiconductor nanorod and a conducting substrate can improve the efficiency of photoelectrodes for hydrogen generation.
plasmonic ZnOs can be fabricated by fs-laser-induced Ag embedded nanostructures, and the plasmonic effect can be used to enhance the efficiency of solar hydrogen generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of plasmonic nanostructure photoelectrocatalysts, which can be applied to solar water splitting for the production of hydrogen.
the development of a new fabrication technique to improve plasmonic nanostructure photoelectrocatalysts.
the fabrication of plasmonic nanostructure photoelectrodies for solar hydrogen generation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plasmonic Zn/Ag nanostructure enhances both the optical absorption and separation of photogenerated charge carriers, which results in a significant improvement of hydrogen generation.
the plasmonics in the photoelectrodes can be utilized as a light-harvesting and electron-collecting layer to increase the efficiency of solar hydrogen generation.
plasmonic ZnOs can be applied as a new collecting layer for photogenerating charge carriers in a solar hydrogen photoelectrode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasmonic nanostructure photoelectrosytem is a promising candidate for efficient solar hydrogen generation.

the plasmonic ZnOs/Ag nanostructures can be used for the fabrication of high-efficiency solar hydrogen photoelectrodes with the ability to generate plasmons at the interface of ZnO/Ag, and thus, to improve charge carrier separation.
plasmonic nanostructure photoelectrosynthesis can be a promising strategy for solar hydrogen generation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasmon-enhanced photoelectrodes are promising candidates for solar hydrogen generation applications.
plasmonic nanostructure photoelectrocatalytic devices can be fabricated in a simple, scalable manner using a fs-laser.
the combination of fs-laser fabrication and plasmonics provides a new strategy for developing highly efficient photoelectrodes in hydrogen generation.
